subtitle.zh: 一次动态图形设计尝试

text.zh:
《人民日报》“山水之间”论坛探讨如何让古典山水意境融入现代生活，以及如何在数字时代重构人与自然的哲学关系。

身处当代都市，一个值得深思的问题是：如何借助新兴数字媒介，让每个人都能抵达心之所向的山水天地？
text.en:
People’s Daily’s “Between Mountains and Waters” forum discusses how the classical “landscape mood” can appear in modern life and how the digital era might build a new nature philosophy.

In today’s urban life, a key question is: how can new digital media let everyone reach the mountain-and-water world they long for?

text.zh:
本项目旨在探寻“每个人心中的山水”。为此，我们首先了解不同个体对山水形态的认知与想象，再以极简的“一笔画”形式，引导参与者勾勒心中的山水意象。

研究对象涵盖风景园林专业的师生，以及非相关专业的学生，通过跨学科的对照研究，探索不同知识背景下山水认知与审美表达的异同。
text.en:
This project aims to find “the mountains-and- waters in each person’s heart.” To do that, we first learn how each user imagines landscape forms. Then, with a very simple method—“one-stroke drawing”—we let users express their own view of mountains and waters. 

Our study group includes landscape-architecture faculty and students, as well as students from non-landscape majors, so we can compare ideas across backgrounds.

text.zh:
通过前期用户调研，我们收集了大量山水轮廓图像，为后续数字生成艺术创作提供了丰富的素材。

参与者只需勾勒心中的山水轮廓，并提供一个专属幸运数字。其中，山水轮廓决定画面的形态构成，幸运数字则用于生成山峦与水体的色彩方案，使每幅作品都呈现出独特的视觉意境。
text.en:
After user surveys, numerous landscape outline images were collected, which can be used for subsequent digital generative art designs. Users are required to draw an outline and provide a lucky number. 

The outline serves as a reference for the image's form, while the lucky number is used to choose the color schemes for mountains and water bodies.

text.zh:
仅凭山水轮廓，尚不足以构筑完整的山水意境。色彩作为中国传统山水画的重要表现语言，承载着独特的审美意蕴与情感表达。

在数字媒介中，色彩通过 RGB、HSV 等数值模型加以呈现。因此，我们引入“幸运数字”作为色彩生成的依据，将个体的数字选择转化为独特的山水配色，赋予每幅作品个性化的视觉意境。
text.en: Using just the landscape outline to construct a landscape is insufficient, as color is a crucial element in Chinese landscape painting. In computers, colors are represented through RGB/HSV values, so users are asked to provide a lucky number for color generation.

subtitle.zh: 一个游戏设计与研究的形式化方法
subtitle.en: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research

text.zh: 这篇文章是由 Robin Hunicke、Marc LeBlanc、和 Robert Zubek 在 2004 年发表的。MDA 的概念最早出现在 GDC 活动的Game Design and Tuning 工作坊。作者们希望为游戏设计、开发和研究者创造一个通用的“语言”。
text.en: This 2004 paper was written by Robin Hunicke, Marc LeBlanc, and Robert Zubek. MDA emerged from Game Design and Tuning Workshops at GDC. The authors wanted a common language for designers, developers, and researchers.

text.zh: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research
text.en: MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research

text.zh: MDA 框架由机制（Mechanics）、动态（Dynamics）与美学体验（Aesthetics）三个层面构成。机制是设计者构建的规则与算法；动态是玩家与游戏系统持续交互过程中涌现的行为；美学体验则是玩家在游戏过程中产生的感受与情绪。然而，功能的实现并不等同于体验的成功。 一套能够正常运行的游戏机制，未必能为玩家带来理想的游戏体验。
text.en: MDA stands for Mechanics, Dynamics, and Aesthetics. Mechanics are the rules and algorithms we design. Dynamics are the behaviors emerging as players interact with those rules over time. Aesthetics are the experiences players have. But a working feature doesn't necessarily create a good experience.

text.zh: 在射击游戏中，武器、弹药与出生点属于机制（Mechanics）；这些规则可能催生蹲点防守、远距离狙击等动态行为（Dynamics），进而让玩家感受到挑战的乐趣，或遭遇挫败与沮丧。这也揭示了设计者与玩家看待同一款游戏时的视角差异：设计者从规则出发构建体验，而玩家则从体验出发感知规则。
text.en: In shooters, weapons, ammunition, and spawn points are Mechanics. They can lead to camping or sniping—Dynamics—which may feel challenging or frustrating. This also reveals why designers and players view the same game differently.

text.zh: 相同的游戏，不同的视角
设计者从规则出发，试图塑造预期的游戏体验；玩家则从自身感受出发，在交互中察觉行为模式，并逐渐理解背后的规则。二者的视角截然不同。然而，如果体验才是设计的最终目标，我们又该如何准确地描述与定义它？
text.en: Designers start with rules and aim for an experience. Players begin with what they feel, notice patterns, and gradually discover the rules. These are different perspectives. but if experience is our goal, how can we describe it precisely?

text.zh: 作者认为，“乐趣（Fun）”这一概念过于笼统，难以准确描述玩家的游戏体验。因此，他们将美学体验（Aesthetics）归纳为八种类型。这里我将重点介绍三个例子：《黑暗之魂》强调挑战（Challenge），《星际拓荒》侧重探索与发现（Discovery），而《我的世界》则为玩家提供了自我表达（Expression）的空间。然而，明确我们希望创造的体验仅仅是设计的起点。我们还需要理解，游戏中实际产生的动态行为（Dynamics）如何支撑，或反过来破坏我们所追求的体验。
text.en: The authors argue that 'fun' is too vague. They identify eight Aesthetics. I'll highlight three examples: Dark Souls emphasizes Challenge, Outer Wilds emphasizes Discovery, and Minecraft supports Expression. But naming the desired experience is only the beginning. We also need to understand how actual Dynamics can support—or undermine—it.

text.zh: 编大富翁的滚雪球效应
《大富翁》便生动地揭示了这一问题。富有的玩家能够购买更多地产，收取更多租金，从而不断扩大领先优势。这种正反馈循环可能让其他玩家逐渐丧失掌控感，陷入无力改变局面的困境。游戏规则虽然正常运作，玩家体验却因此受到损害。那么，设计者究竟可以从何处着手改变这一局面？
text.en: Monopoly illustrates this problem. Wealthy players buy more property, collect more rent, and extend their lead. This positive feedback loop can make others feel powerless. The rules work, but the experience suffers. So what can designers change?

text.zh: 一种方法是引入追赶奖励机制，帮助落后的玩家缩小差距；另一种方法则是对领先的富有玩家施加惩罚或征收税费。然而，这两种方式都无法保证游戏体验一定得到改善。我们仍需通过反复的游戏测试与规则调优，确保实际体验符合预期的设计目标。MDA 框架不仅能够帮助我们改进现有游戏，也能为全新游戏的设计提供指导。
text.en: One option is bonuses that help players catch up. Another is a penalty or tax on wealthy players. But neither guarantees a better game. We must playtest and tune the rules against the intended experience. MDA helps fix existing games—and design new ones.

text.zh: 论文中的 AI 案例展示了 MDA 框架在新游戏设计中的应用。一个简单的照看孩子游戏，只需要基础的躲藏行为和富有表现力的角色反应；卡通风格的版本则加入了多个角色与时间压力；而潜行游戏需要更复杂的感知、寻路与协同机制。尽管这些游戏都围绕“寻找与追逐”这一核心概念展开，但不同的预期体验，对 AI 系统提出了截然不同的设计要求。那么，我们又该如何判断这些系统是否真正达到了设计目标？
text.en: The paper's AI example shows that second use. A simple babysitting game needs basic hiding and expressive reactions. A cartoon version adds multiple characters and time pressure. A stealth game needs perception, navigation, and coordination. The idea is still finding and chasing, but different desired experiences require different AI systems. How do we know if they work?

text.zh: MDA 是一个循环，而非一份清单
text.en: MDA is a loop, not a list

text.zh: 这正是迭代设计的意义所在。我们首先制定游戏规则，观察玩家的实际行为，评估由此产生的游戏体验，再据此调整和优化游戏机制（Mechanics），如此循环往复。MDA 不仅是一套用于描述游戏的概念框架，更是一种帮助我们持续改进游戏设计的方法。
text.en: That's where iteration matters. We design rules, observe real play, evaluate the resulting experience, and tune the Mechanics. Then we repeat. MDA is not just a set of labels; it helps us improve games.

lead.zh: 游戏设计 / 美术 / 程序开发

bio.zh: 我叫吴浩，具有建筑学科背景，研究空间与叙事的有机关卡。探究不同的玩法，立足于系统理论，向外探索有趣的，实验性的玩法，目标是为爱好的玩家创造有趣的体验！
bio.en: My name is Hao Wu. With a background in architecture, I explore organic level design that seamlessly integrates space and narrative. Grounded in systems thinking, I experiment with innovative gameplay mechanics to create unique and engaging experiences for passionate players.
